gloss: step, go straight on; on the right path (hence happy); (particle) who, which, that
summary: The root of the step and the way walked. The verb is to go straight on, or to lead someone on, in a way; אֲשֻׁר is a step; and אַשְׁרֵי, "the right goings of…!", declares someone on the right path, above all the one who walks in Yahweh's way and the one whose sin he has forgiven; since it goes well with such a one, it is also the call "happy!". From the same verb comes the calling itself: to count or call someone on the right path, and so fortunate, happy. The particle אֲשֶׁר, "who, which, that", the Hebrew Bible's commonest way of joining one clause to a word in another, goes back in the related languages to a noun for a footstep, trace or place, which Akkadian also uses for "where". The tree תְּאַשּׁוּר is built on the root too, though how is not clear.

words.gloss: who, which, that; where; because; so that
words.summary: Never inflected. It marks the clause after it as describing a word before it, or as standing in for a noun itself; a pronoun or שָׁם "there" inside the clause often shows the part the word plays in it. The shorter שֶׁ־ does the same work (Psa 146:5; 137:8).

senses.definition: Joins a clause to a noun before it, to say which one, or what is true of it.

evidence.note: "the man whom he had formed" (אֲשֶׁר יָצָר).
"the waters that were under the expanse": the clause need have no verb.
Yahweh "who took me … and who spoke to me and who swore to me".
אֶהְיֶה אֲשֶׁר אֶהְיֶה, "I will be who I will be".

senses.gloss: on which, where (with a pronoun or שָׁם)
senses.definition: A pronoun in the clause, or שָׁם "there", points back to the noun and says how it stands in the clause: "the place which you stand on it" is "the place on which you stand".

evidence.note: הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה עוֹמֵד עָלָיו: "the place on which you are standing".
הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר הָיָה שָׁם אָהֳלֹה: "the place where his tent had been".
"the land that you are lying on (עָלֶיהָ)".

senses.definition: With no noun before it, the clause itself names a person or thing: the one who, those who, whatever.

evidence.note: אֶת־אֲשֶׁר עַל־בֵּיתוֹ: "the one who was over his house".
"I will teach you what you shall speak".
"whom you bless is blessed, and whom you curse is cursed".
"Noah and those who were with him in the ark".
"whomever you find your gods with".

senses.definition: After a verb of seeing or knowing, introduces what is seen or known.

evidence.note: "Saul saw that he was succeeding greatly".
"so that you will know that Yahweh distinguishes between Egypt and Israel".

senses.definition: Gives the reason for what has been said; with יַעַן, "because of the fact that".

evidence.note: "God has given me my reward, because I gave my maidservant to my husband".
"We are guilty concerning our brother, because we saw the distress of his soul".
יַעַן אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתָ: "because you have done this thing".
יַעַן אֲשֶׁר מִלֵּא אַחֲרֵי יַהְוֶה: Caleb, "because he has fully followed Yahweh".

senses.definition: Gives the purpose or the result; with לֹא, "so that … not".

evidence.note: "I will make them hear my words, that they may learn to fear me".
אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִשְׁמְעוּ: "so that they will not understand each other's language".
"that it may go well with you, and that you may multiply greatly".

senses.gloss: with a preposition: as, where, than, until
senses.definition: Joined to a preposition, the particle makes the clause its object: כַּאֲשֶׁר "as (that which)", בַּאֲשֶׁר "in (that which)", מֵאֲשֶׁר "from or than (that which)", עַד אֲשֶׁר "until".

evidence.note: כַּאֲשֶׁר יִשָּׂא־אִישׁ אֶת־בְּנוֹ: "as a man carries his son".

senses.definition: Compares one action with another, or, in narrative, sets the time of one by another.

evidence.note: "just as Yahweh your God did to the Sea of Reeds".
וַיְהִי כַּאֲשֶׁר רָאָה: "when Jacob saw Rachel".
"the more they afflicted him, the more he multiplied".

senses.definition: "In (the place) where", and from that, "in that, because".

evidence.note: בַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא־שָׁם: "where he is".
"where you lodge, I will lodge".
בַּאֲשֶׁר אַתְּ־אִשְׁתּוֹ: "because you are his wife".

senses.definition: The preposition מִן with the clause: comparison ("more than those whom"), or the source ("from what").

evidence.note: "more than those he killed in his life".
"from whatever his hand can reach".

senses.definition: Up to the time when.

evidence.note: "until your brother's fury turns away".
The Septuagint's ὅς for אֲשֶׁר in "the man who has not walked".
ὅ for אֲשֶׁר: "the water which was under the firmament".

words.gloss: right going; (אַשְׁרֵי) on the right path is…!, hence happy is…!
words.summary: Found only in the plural, as the exclamation אַשְׁרֵי "the right goings of…!", "on the right path is…!", or with a pronoun (אַשְׁרֶיךָ "on the right path are you!"). Since it goes well with the one on the right path, it also says "happy is…!", and where no path is in view, as of plain good fortune, that is all it says. It is said of people, a people and once a land, never of God.

senses.gloss: on the right path is…!; happy is…!
senses.definition: Declares someone on the right path, and so well off, and in the same breath says what that rests on: the way they walk, whom they trust, what has been done for them.

evidence.note: "The right goings of the man who has not walked in the counsel of the wicked, nor stood in the way of sinners": the path is in the verse itself.
אַשְׁרֶיךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל: "On the right path are you, Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by Yahweh?"
"One keeping the law, on the right path is he" (אַשְׁרֵהוּ).

senses.gloss: of one who walks in Yahweh's way
senses.definition: The one on the right path is the one whose way is blameless, who walks in Yahweh's teaching and keeps it.

evidence.note: "On the right path are the blameless of way, the ones walking in the teaching of Yahweh".
"On the right path is everyone who fears Yahweh, who walks in his ways".
Wisdom's: "on the right path is the man who listens to me".
"On the right path is the man who … keeps the Sabbath … and keeps his hand from doing any evil".

senses.definition: The one on the right path takes refuge in Yahweh, waits for him, and has him for help.

evidence.note: "Taste and see that Yahweh is good; on the right path is the man who takes refuge in him".
"On the right path are all who take refuge in him": in the son.
"On the right path is the one who waits and reaches the 1,335 days".

senses.gloss: of one forgiven or corrected by God
senses.definition: The one on the right path is the one whose sin is covered and not reckoned, or whom God corrects and teaches.

evidence.note: "On the right path is the one whose transgression is lifted, whose sin is covered".
"On the right path is the man to whom Yahweh reckons no guilt".
"On the right path is the man God corrects".

senses.definition: The secondary sense, where no path is in view: plain good fortune, said of Solomon's servants, the man with a quiver full of sons, a land with a noble king, even the one who repays Babylon.

evidence.note: "Happy your men, happy these servants of yours who stand before you continually".
Of a land: "happy are you, land, whose king is a son of nobles".
"Blessed (μακάριοι) are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven" quotes Psa 32:1.
"Blessed (μακάριος) is the man whose sin the Lord will not reckon" quotes Psa 32:2.
Paul names it the μακαρισμός, the "blessedness", of which David speaks.
The Septuagint's μακάριοι for אַשְׁרֵי.
μακάριος for אַשְׁרֵי.

parallels.note: blameless: those declared on the right path are the blameless of way.

phrases.gloss: on the right path is the man (who…)

words.gloss: go straight on; lead on; call on the right path (happy)

senses.definition: Walk on in a way.

evidence.note: וְאִשְׁרוּ בְּדֶרֶךְ בִּינָה: "and go straight on in the way of understanding".

stems.gloss: go on; lead on, guide; call on the right path (happy)

senses.definition: Walk on in a way, set beside "go" (בּוֹא).

evidence.note: "On the path of the wicked do not go, and do not walk on (אַל־תְּאַשֵּׁר) in the way of evil men".

senses.definition: Make someone, or one's heart, go on in a way; of leaders, to guide a people, rightly or astray.

evidence.note: וְאַשֵּׁר בַּדֶּרֶךְ לִבֶּךָ: "lead your heart on in the way".
מְאַשְּׁרֶיךָ מַתְעִים: "those who lead you lead you astray".
"The guides of this people mislead them".
אַשְּׁרוּ חָמוֹץ, beside "seek justice": set right the oppressor, or lead on the oppressed; חָמוֹץ occurs only here.

senses.gloss: call on the right path; call happy, count fortunate
senses.definition: Say אַשְׁרֵי of someone: declare them on the right path, and so call them happy and praise their good fortune.

evidence.note: Leah: בְּאָשְׁרִי כִּי אִשְּׁרוּנִי בָּנוֹת, "In my right going! For the daughters will call me on the right path" (in the secondary sense, "happy").
"Her sons rise up and call her on the right path; her husband also praises her".
"All the nations will call you on the right path, for you will be a land of delight".
"Now we call the arrogant on the right path": the complaint Yahweh answers.
"all nations will call him on the right path", beside "bless themselves in him".

stems.gloss: be led; be set on the right path (made happy)

senses.definition: Be the ones guided.

evidence.note: וּמְאֻשָּׁרָיו מְבֻלָּעִים: "and those led by them are swallowed up".

senses.gloss: be set or counted on the right path; be made happy
senses.definition: Be the one of whom אַשְׁרֵי is said.

evidence.note: Wisdom is a tree of life to those who take hold of her, "and those who hold her fast are set on the right path", after "all her paths are peace" (Pro 3:17).
"he will be counted on the right path in the land", after "on the right path is the one who considers the lowly" (Psa 41:2).
Mary's "all generations will call me happy (μακαριοῦσίν)" is in the words of Leah's (Gen 30:13).
The Septuagint's μακαρίζουσίν for אִשְּׁרוּנִי.

parallels.note: praise: calling someone on the right path is praising them.
bless: in Psa 72:17 the nations bless themselves in the king and call him on the right path, two different words side by side.

opposites.note: lead astray: Isaiah's leaders lead the people on, but astray.

words.summary: Always plural or with a pronoun ("my steps", "his step"), and only in poetry. BDB lists the same occurrences under the spellings אֲשׁוּר and אַשֻּׁר.

senses.definition: Where the foot goes, set beside "feet" and "footsteps": and so a person's course, which may keep to Yahweh's way or turn from it.

evidence.note: "My steps have held to your tracks; my footsteps (פְעָמַי) have not slipped".
"My feet had almost turned aside; my steps had almost slipped".
"He set my feet on a rock, he made my steps firm".
"The law of his God is in his heart; his steps do not slip".
"nor have our steps turned aside from your way".
"My foot has held to his steps; his way I have kept and not turned aside".
"the prudent considers his step".

words.summary: A noun with the prefix תְּ־ on this root. How a tree's name joins the root's sense of going straight on is not clear; the tree itself is named only in lists of trees, so which one it is cannot be fixed from scripture.

senses.gloss: a tree, named with the cypress and the plane
senses.definition: One of the trees Yahweh will set in the wilderness, and one of "the glory of Lebanon" that will beautify his sanctuary.

evidence.note: "the cypress, the plane and the תְּאַשּׁוּר together", planted in the Arabah.
The same three trees, "the glory of Lebanon", brought to beautify the place of the sanctuary.

שֵׁן בַּת־אֲשֻׁרִים, the ivory of Tyre's deck, may be ivory set in this wood if the letters are read as one word (בִּתְאַשֻּׁרִים, "in תְּאַשּׁוּר wood"); as divided in the text, "the daughter of Ashurim".

words.summary: Found only once, in Leah's cry at Asher's birth.

senses.definition: A course going right, which others will call on the right path; so good fortune, happiness.

evidence.note: בְּאָשְׁרִי: "In my right going!", followed by the verb: "the daughters will call me on the right path".

words.summary: Biblical Aramaic, where Hebrew's שׁ answers to Aramaic ת. The house of God is to be built "on its place".

senses.definition: The spot where something is or belongs.

evidence.note: "no place was found for them".
"let the house of God be built on its place" (עַל־אַתְרֵהּ).
בָּאתַר דְּנָה: "after this".

senses.definition: A land or district.

evidence.note: The Peshitta's לאתרא for "to the region of Galilee".
"to their country".

cognates.note: The verb's eighth stem is "follow someone's footsteps".

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 18, art. اثر, أَثَرٌ
p. 18, art. اثر, 8 اِئْتَثَرَهُ "he followed his footsteps"

cognates.gloss: footprint; sole of the foot; step; trodden path; sign; remains
cognates.note: Footprint and step together, as Hebrew's אֲשֻׁר is a step.

evidence.note: Sets beside it אֲשֻׁר "step", Arabic أثر and Syriac ܐܬܪܐ "place".

cognates.gloss: place, site; abode; region; (construct ašar, as a conjunction) where
cognates.note: The construct ašar introduces a clause, "where": a noun for place doing a particle's work, as אֲשֶׁר does.

evidence.note: st. constr. as a conjunction with the subjunctive, "where".
where, wherever.

cognates.note: A verb of going, as אָשַׁר "go straight on".
The Phoenician relative particle, doing אֲשֶׁר's work ("in the place that I built"); its link to ʾṯr is not shown in the source.

cognates.gloss: he exulted, rejoiced, especially in wealth; behaved insolently, ungratefully
cognates.note: The nearest of any cognate to the secondary sense "happy", but by the sound correspondences Arabic ش is the older ś, Hebrew שׂ, not the שׁ that אֶשֶׁר is read with. The consonants alone cannot tell ש from שׂ, so the words for the right path could hide a root ʾśr; against it, the Arabic is mostly blame (insolent, unthankful exulting) where the Hebrew is praise, and the reading tradition has shin throughout, the name Asher too.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 61, art. اشر, أَشِرَ
evidence.note: "He exulted … and behaved insolently and unthankfully"; or "he rejoiced, and rested his mind upon things agreeable with natural desire".

doctrine.statement: David declares on the right path the one whose transgression is lifted and whose sin is covered, the man to whom Yahweh reckons no guilt (Psa 32:1–2). He is set on the right path by what has been done for him, not by what he has done. Paul reads the Psalm this way: David speaks of the blessedness (μακαρισμός) of the man to whom God reckons righteousness apart from works, and he quotes both verses (Rom 4:6–8).

The Psalms open by declaring on the right path the man who has not walked in the counsel of the wicked (Psa 1:1), and Psalm 119 the blameless of way who walk in the teaching of Yahweh (Psa 119:1); Psalm 128 says the same of everyone who fears Yahweh and walks in his ways (Psa 128:1). The same root names the steps of that walk: the man with his God's law in his heart does not slip in his steps (Psa 37:31), and it is Yahweh who sets the feet on a rock and makes the steps firm (Psa 40:3). In scripture's use, then, to be on the right path, and so happy, is to keep to Yahweh's way, and that course is kept by his law and by his hand.

Psalm 2 records Yahweh's decree to his king, "You are my son; today I have begotten you" (Psa 2:7), warns the kings to kiss the son, and ends: "on the right path are all who take refuge in him" (Psa 2:12). The New Testament reads the decree of Jesus (Act 13:33; Heb 1:5), so the right path the Psalm declares belongs to those who take refuge in him.

note: Kept as one root: the particle, the step, the verb, the words for the right path and the tree. The cognates join the particle to a noun for footstep, trace or place (Brockelmann sets אֲשֶׁר beside Syriac ܐܬܪܐ, Arabic أثر and Akkadian ašru; Akkadian ašar "where" is the noun doing a particle's work), and Ge'ez አሠר and Dillmann join "footprint" to the step אֲשֻׁר; Ugaritic ʾṯr is a verb "march". No dictionary consulted links אֶשֶׁר to these; within scripture the piel carries both "lead on" and "call happy" (Gen 30:13 has the noun and the verb together). Scripture ties אַשְׁרֵי to the path: of the 42 verses with אַשְׁרֵי or its suffixed forms, 10 have a word of way, walking, foot or step in the verse itself (Psa 1:1, 119:1, 128:1, 84:6, Pro 8:32, 20:7 among them) and 5 more in the verse beside it, where 8.5% of Old Testament verses have one (as of Psalms, Proverbs and Job alone): about 3.6 of 42 by chance, p ≈ 0.002. Unpointed, אשרי is both "on the right path is…!" and "my steps" (אֲשֻׁרַי, Psa 17:5, 73:2; Job 31:7). So "on the right path" is taken as the primary sense of אֶשֶׁר, אֹשֶׁר and the piel and pual that call or count someone so, and "happy" as the secondary sense that follows from it; on that reading the footprint cognates share their meaning and are named on them. The reading rests on scripture's use and is to be refined as more evidence comes to light. Against it, Arabic أَشِرَ "exult" (ar-ashira) is closer to "happy" but has the wrong sibilant. "In order, prospering" belongs to another root, ישר (Akkadian išaru, Ugaritic yšr, with š, not ṯ). Open lead: Akkadian ašāru, perhaps "muster, check, take care of", not confirmed; CAD A/2 to consult. The tree תְּאַשּׁוּר is kept though its link to the root's sense is not clear. Left out, for their own entries: the names אָשֵׁר Asher and the gentilic אָשֵׁרִי (Jdg 1:32), whom Leah names with this root's words (Gen 30:13), so his entry should link back here; אֲשֵׁרָה Asherah, a goddess's name and her cult pole (Ugaritic ʾaṯrt), whose entry should weigh a link to this root; and אַשּׁוּר Assyria, from the Akkadian city name Aššur, which belongs to another word. BDB lists the same occurrences under both אֲשׁוּר and אַשֻּׁר, one word here. CAD and Leslau not consulted. The particle's senses are illustrated, not exhaustive: 5,500 tokens. Scripture's Aramaic אֲתַר and the Peshitta's ܐܬܪܐ are kept as words of this entry, under their own root אתר (Aramaic ת for Hebrew ש, both from ṯ). Leads for ܐܬܪܐ not yet followed to verses: Payne Smith p. 33 and Brockelmann pp. 55–56 give "region, country" and, as a conjunction, "where"; Brockelmann sets it beside Arabic أثر, Akkadian ašru and Hebrew אֲשֶׁר; SEDRA lexeme 324.
